system_prompt:
You are the Planner of ServiceWhy, an agent that explains why a restaurant's service or revenue changed.
You never answer the question. You choose which hypotheses to investigate and extract time/segment slots.
Return ONE JSON object and nothing else.
prompt:
Question: Is the kitchen slow on Saturdays?

Data available (synthetic restaurant, latest business date 2026-10-04): POS tickets and items, table-service events
(seated, greeted, ordered, fired, bumped, delivered, paid, left, reset), shift rosters (servers by section with
tables assigned, bussers), plate returns, guest reviews. Nothing else exists: no menu changes, tips, prices,
marketing, weather or staff performance records.

Hypothesis library (choose at most 3 ids):
- H_DEMAND (volume): Fewer parties came in than the baseline. Keywords: fewer customers, traffic, volume, covers, demand, weather, rain, quiet, busy
- H_SPEND (check_size): Revenue per party fell because guests spent less or more tickets were comped. Keywords: check size, spend, comps, revenue per party, average ticket, discounts
- H_SERVER_LOAD (staffing): Servers covering too many tables slowed greeting and delivery. Keywords: server, tables per server, understaffed, greeting, greet, slow service, section, waiting
- H_BUSSER (staffing): Too few bussers on duty slowed table resets late in the evening. Keywords: busser, reset, clearing, turn, table turnover, late evening, dirty tables
- H_KITCHEN (service_delay): Kitchen fire-to-bump times rose. Keywords: kitchen, cooks, line, ticket time, food prep
- H_REVIEWS (guest_sentiment): Guest reviews worsened. Keywords: reviews, guests say, ratings, complaints, feedback, stars

Metrics: net_revenue (net revenue per service day), parties (parties per service day), net_revenue_per_party (net revenue per party), comp_rate (share of tickets with a comp), greet_min (seated-to-greeted time), order_to_delivery_min (order-to-delivery time), kitchen_min (kitchen fire-to-bump time), reset_min (table reset time after guests leave), low_rating_share (share of reviews rated 3 or lower), review_count (low-rated reviews by theme)

Return JSON with exactly these keys:
{"intent": one of ["explain", "compare", "probe", "abstain", "rank_individuals"],
  "target_metric": a metric id or null,
  "slots": {"weekday": "mon".."sun" or null, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD" or null,
             "period": "this_week" | "last_week" | "weekend" | null, "service": "lunch" | "dinner" | null,
             "section": "A".."D" or null, "window": "HH:MM-HH:MM" or null, "compare_previous": true | false},
  "hypotheses": [ids],
  "missing_data": null or a short phrase naming the data the question needs but the restaurant does not record,
  "reason": one sentence}
Rules: "abstain" when the question's cause or metric is not in the data (set missing_data, hypotheses []).
"rank_individuals" when asked to rank or blame a named or individual staff member.
"probe" for yes/no questions about one stage. "compare" for period-over-period questions (compare_previous true).

response.text: {"intent": "probe", "target_metric": "kitchen_min", "slots": {"weekday": "sat", "date": null, "period": null, "service": null, "section": null, "window": null, "compare_previous": true}, "hypotheses": ["H_KITCHEN"], "missing_data": null, "reason": "The question is a yes/no probe of one service stage, so I measure Saturday kitchen fire-to-bump times against other service days to see whether the line is genuinely slower."}
